parts.text: Calcium is an element in Group II of the Periodic Table.

ms.label: 2(b)
ms.text:
M1 metallic
M2 positive ions / cations
M3 sea of electrons / mobile electrons / delocalised electrons
M4 attraction between positive ions and electrons

parts.label: c
parts.text: (c) When a piece of calcium is added to some cold water containing universal indicator a reaction takes place.

ms.label: 2(c)(i)
ms.text:
M1 effervescence
M2 solid dissolves
M3 solution turns blue

ms.label: 2(d)(ii)
ms.text:
2Ca + O2 → 2CaO
M1 CaO as only product
M2 correct equation

parts.label: e
parts.text: (e) Crystals of hydrated calcium nitrate contain water molecules. The formula of hydrated calcium nitrate is Ca(NO 3 ) 2 •xH 2 O. x is a whole number.

parts.label: ii
parts.text: (ii) When hydrated calcium nitrate is heated gently, the following reaction occurs. Ca(NO 3 ) 2 •xH 2 O Ca(NO 3 ) 2 + xH 2 O A sample of hydrated calcium nitrate is heated gently. 3.28 g of Ca(NO 3 ) 2 forms and the mass of the crystals decreases by 1.44 g. [M r : Ca(NO 3 ) 2 , 164; H 2 O, 18] Determine the value of x in Ca(NO 3 ) 2 •xH 2 O using the following steps. • Calculate the number of moles of Ca(NO 3 ) 2 that remain. .............................. mol • Calculate the number of moles of H 2 O given off. .............................. mol • Determine the value of x. x = .............................. [3]
